correctness.rationale: The exact Bernoulli/Fourier identity uses Hwang–Kuriki eq. (74). Under the sinusoidal alternative, all Fourier means except j=k_n vanish and all nonexceptional modes have E[n|hat-phi|^2]=1. For each fixed low block the real covariance becomes precisely I/2 once k_n>2J, hence a bounded-array joint CLT. Summability of j^(-2m) bounds the remaining infinite tail uniformly. The exceptional coefficient is epsilon/2+O_p(n^(-1/2)), yielding a deterministic critical translation or divergence. Null CDF continuity proves power limits, Hoeffding's bound proves TV separation. A standalone finite numerical checker passed 56 supporting assertions; it is not used as an asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The priority claim is only the moving-frequency triangular-array limit, sharp n/k_n^(2m) boundary, and cross-order power hierarchy, not prior Bernoulli kernels, null quadratic series or ordinary Sobolev principles. Actual primary full-text comparisons with Hwang–Kuriki 2024, Henze–Nikitin 2002 and García-Portugués–Paindaveine–Verdebout 2021 show different quantifiers and alternative classes. Published fixed-mode power experiments and fixed-shape local alternatives do not imply the moving-frequency result without separate uniform tail and triangular-array arguments. Residual possibility of another unlocated general theorem remains.

value.rationale: For one natural n^(1/3) oscillation scale, the m=1 test has power approaching one, each higher fixed order asymptotically rejects at only its nominal level, and total variation of the n-sample experiments approaches one exponentially. This precise sharp spectral oversmoothing gap and its critical translated law are motivated properties of a published multilevel GOF toolbox, not a cosmetic parameter change or bare numerical result.
